button.title: Button & IconButton
button.purpose: Triggers an action on the current surface (save, submit, open, delete). Navigation between pages is a link, not a Button.
use: Committing or cancelling a task (forms, dialogs, toolbars).
Icon-only actions in dense toolbars (IconButton + aria-label + Tooltip).
avoid: Choosing a filter, sort or scope → Chip (variant="advanced").
Switching views or sections → Segmented or Tabs.
Navigating to another page → a link or Sidebar item.
api: main · flat · overlay (overlay only on imagery/dark media)
primary · tertiary (default pair) · secondary (rare) · accent (promoted) · danger · danger-subtle · positive · positive-subtle · surface
an icon name ("icon-plus-line") or a node (<Icon name size />)
defaults to aria-label: shown after 1s of hover, at once on keyboard focus, never on touch; text for a longer hint; false only beside a visible label
do: Give each surface exactly one Primary button, the main CTA.
Use Tertiary for every other action; it is the most common level.
Pair actions as Tertiary (dismiss) + Primary (commit), with Primary last, on the right.
Use Danger or Danger-Subtle for irreversible actions (Delete, Discard).
Start labels with a verb and keep them to 1–3 words ("Save changes", "Invite").
Disable a button only while its precondition is unmet, and explain why nearby (help text, validation).
Show progress on the button itself ("Deleting…") and disable siblings while it runs.
Use Flat Primary (Button/Icon-Flat Small) for close and dismiss icon buttons in Dialog, ModalForm and Side Panel headers (harness: button/flat-level).
Size buttons by layout: a full-width button (mobile CTA, empty state, stacked form footer) is Medium or larger; Small buttons (2xs · xs · sm) hug their label and align to the start.

On a phone, put the main action in the footer as Large (lg) full-width buttons, Primary on top and at most one Tertiary alternative below; small sizes (2xs–sm) always hug their label (harness: button/small-full-width).

Let every icon-only action show its name as a tooltip after 1s of hover (IconButton does it by default; custom icon-only controls spread useIconTooltip(label).bind() and render .tooltip) (harness: icon-button/tooltip, button/icon-only-raw).
dont: Don't use Secondary as the default second button. It is a rare highlight (e.g. a pressed toolbar toggle); justify it with zen-allow-secondary.
Don't use Accent for ordinary primaries; reserve it for promoted CTAs (upsell, onboarding, the floating feedback action).
Don't put two Primary buttons side by side.
Don't use a Button to open a filter/sort list.
Don't ship an IconButton without aria-label.
Don't use vague labels ("OK", "Click here") for consequential actions.
Don't use "OK", "Yes", "Submit" or "Click here"; name the outcome (harness: button/vague-label).

Don't stretch a Small button (2xs · xs · sm) across its container: a thin, wide button reads as a divider or input, and the label floats in empty space. Use size md, or let it hug (harness: button/small-full-width).
Don't label a Button "Filters" or give it a filter icon to open filters; that trigger is a Chip (harness: button/filter-is-chip).
Don't draw a Back button or IconButton with a left arrow on mobile/tablet; use icon-chevron-left-line-medium (harness: navigation/back-chevron).
Don't build an icon-only action from a raw <button> + <Icon>, and don't pass tooltip={false} unless a visible label sits right beside it.

Don't use XSmall / 2XSmall text buttons for ordinary actions (examples, cards, toolbars, forms, footers) — use sm or larger. XSmall/2XSmall are only for special compact pills beside a row, like the App Store's Get · Install · Open (harness: button/compact-size-special).
a11y: Native <button>; Enter/Space activate. Focus ring is Focus/Accent (3px).
IconButton requires aria-label; add a Tooltip with the same text for sighted users.
Toggle buttons expose aria-pressed.
Minimum hit target 24px (2xs); prefer ≥ 32px (sm) for pointer, 40px (md) for touch.
content: Sentence case, verb first.
Match the dialog title's verb in its primary action ("Delete project?" → "Delete project").

rules.summary: Secondary is a rare highlight; default to Primary (main CTA) or Tertiary.
Filter, sort and scope pickers are Chip (variant=advanced), never buttons.
Accent is for promoted CTAs (upsell, onboarding) only.
Irreversible actions (Delete, Remove, Discard) use Danger or Danger-Subtle.
Icon-only buttons need an aria-label.
An IconButton does something: it has onClick (or href, or type="submit"), unless it is a Menu trigger (the Menu wires it).
Icon-only buttons show their name as a tooltip after 1s of hover (at once on keyboard focus); IconButton does it by default — turn it off only when a visible label sits right beside it.
An icon-only action is an IconButton (or uses useIconTooltip), so it gets the Zen tokens, focus ring and the 1s name tooltip — not a hand-built <button> with just an <Icon>.
Back actions on mobile and tablet use a left chevron (icon-chevron-left-line-medium), never a left arrow.
Button/Flat has levels primary · secondary · accent · danger · positive only; any other level falls back to the Main look (border + shadow). Close / dismiss icon buttons are Flat Primary.
Small buttons (2xs · xs · sm) always hug their label; a full-width button is size md or larger (Figma CTA = Medium, full width).
FileIcon identifies a file's type; it is never the icon of a button or action.
Labels start with a verb and name the outcome ("Save changes"), never "OK", "Submit" or "Click here".
One Main Primary per surface: never two Primary buttons side by side (Flat/Overlay levels are exempt).
Text buttons at XSmall/2XSmall are for special compact pills only — like the App Store's Get / Install / Open next to a list row. Actions in examples, cards, toolbars and forms use sm or larger.
Removing the outline on focus requires a replacement ring (Focus/Accent) on the same element.

A deprecated prop still works but has a canonical name (onValueChange, onCheckedChange, checked, selected, level…); apps get a warning with the replacement. (App mode only; the repo migrates gradually.)
Icon names must exist (1,598 names that follow the Figma layer path, e.g. icon-search-medium-line); search them instead of guessing (MCP search_icons, or the Iconography page).

Every interaction a Zen control offers works: no no-op handlers (`() => {}`, `() => undefined`), which leave a field that ignores typing and ↑/↓ or a Dismiss that stays. Chat has chat/no-locked-interaction.

Repo examples, playgrounds and templates: every action does something when pressed. Flags a `Button` or `<button>` without onClick / href / type="submit" (IconButton: icon-button/needs-action), an action object ({ icon, label }) in leading, trailing, action, primaryAction, secondaryAction, subAction or actions without onClick, and pressable items whose list has no onSelect / onNavigate / onItemClick / onValueChange. Documented defaults pass: Dialog, ModalForm, SidePanel and BottomSheet actions close the overlay; a Menu opens from its trigger. Apps are not judged.

chip.title: Chip / Pill
chip.purpose: Compact, selectable tokens. Advanced chips are the Zen filter control: each owns a Popover of options.
use: Filter/sort/scope/status/owner pickers (variant="advanced" + popoverItems).
Toggleable topic pills (variant="normal", aria-pressed).
Counts in dense layouts (variant="number-only"): without onClick or selected it is a static count, not a button.
avoid: Primary actions → Button.
Read-only labels or statuses → Badge.
Values inside an input → Tag.
api: selected styling (select is the deprecated alias); chevron only — the chip opens its own Popover only with popoverItems (or onPopoverCreate)
a chip that opens a Bottom Sheet or filter panel; popoverOpen flips the chevron
keyboard: Toggle the chip or open its list
Close the Popover and return focus
do: Use one Advanced chip per filter dimension (Status, Owner, Date).
Show a count with a Number-only chip and no handler: it renders as a static count (Figma: a compact indicator for counts). Give it onClick or selected only when pressing the number does something.
Show the chosen value as the chip label for single selection; show the counter for multiple.
Wire onClearSelection so Delete/Backspace and the × clear the filter.
Offer "Clear all" (Tertiary button) when two or more filters are active.
Keep Advanced chips' Popover open while toggling multiple options (popoverMultiple).
Show the count on multiple-selection chips (harness: chip/multiple-needs-count).

On a phone, keep filter chips in one horizontally scrolling row (no wrapping) and open choices in an Action Bottom Sheet instead of a Popover; show the result count with a plural label and offer Clear filters on an empty result.
dont: Don't use Secondary or any Button to open a filter list.
Don't use Segmented to filter data (Segmented switches views).
Don't give a Normal or Number-only chip popoverItems.
Don't wrap chips inside another button.
a11y: Chip is a <button>; the Popover is a listbox with role=option items. A Number-only chip without onClick or selected is a count: a <span>, out of the tab order, with no hover.
↓ opens, Escape closes and returns focus, Delete/Backspace clears (aria-keyshortcuts).
Topic pills expose aria-pressed.
content: Label the chip with the dimension ("Status") until a value is picked, then the value ("Done").

rules.summary: Filter, sort and scope pickers are Chip (variant=advanced), never buttons.
Only Chip variant=advanced opens a Popover.
A multiple-selection Chip shows how many values are active with selectionCount.

input.title: Input fields
input.purpose: Collect a single value from the user. All fields share Label → Field → Help-Text anatomy and the Leading/Trailing slots.
use: Free text → InputField; long text → TextAreaField.
One option from a list → SelectField (≤ 10 options), otherwise AutocompleteField.
Dates → DateField; quantities → NumberField (steppers).
Inline editable titles → HeadingField: one line for short names (a board, a file), multiline when titles run long (documents, announcements, tasks).
Formatted long text (announcements, descriptions) → RichTextField.
avoid: Searching/filtering content → Search.
Binary settings → Toggle or Checkbox.
2–5 mutually exclusive visible options → RadioButton group or Segmented.
api: small · medium · large · xlarge (xlarge uses Heading/4 text)
always label; help text under the field
label · labelOptional · labelTooltip · labelAction (InputLabel optional / tooltip / action / disabled)
(Optional) marker, 12px info icon with a Tooltip, right-aligned Body/Small/Bold action
Theme neutral · warning · positive (error = negative); Icon on/off; Character-Limitation text or `true` + maxLength
shows the value, no fill, Border/Neutral/Subtle
decorative, picker (options) or action (onClick); interactive overrides per use case
align · value · onValueChange · min · max · step
value / defaultValue (HTML) · onValueChange(html, text) · editorBar · editorBarTheme · characterLimit
Figma Input/Richtext + Control-Bar; label above the bar
default (minus) · success (check) · wrong (x); Body/Small/Regular, list gap XSmall
h1–h3 (Heading/1–3); one line by default, multiline wraps and grows (Figma Inputted-Multi-Line)
do: Always render a visible label; use aria-label only when the context already labels the field (e.g. a Share link row).
Validate on blur or submit, then show error text that says how to fix it.
Use Read-only for values the user may see but not change.
Use helpTheme="warning" for a soft caution and "positive" to confirm a check passed; reserve Negative for `error`.

Make a labelled Leading/Trailing slot a picker (options) for units, country codes or account types, or an action (onClick) such as show password; set interactive={false} when it is purely informative.
Clamp NumberField with min/max; steppers disable at the bounds.
Keep help text to one line; move long guidance to InputConditions or docs.
Show requirement rules (passwords, handles) as InputConditions under the field: Default before typing, then Success/Wrong live as the value changes.
RichTextField: read content through onValueChange(html, text), store the HTML and render it through your sanitizer.
RichTextField: keep the Control-Bar (editorBar) unless the surface is tiny.

RichTextField keeps its own undo history: Undo / Redo (⌘Z, ⇧⌘Z, Ctrl+Y) step through this field's edits only and are disabled while there is nothing to undo or redo; replacing `value` from outside (clearing after Post) starts a new history.
HeadingField: set multiline when a title can run past one line, so it wraps instead of scrolling out of view.
dont: Don't use Disabled on inputs; Zen inputs have Read-only only.
Don't use placeholder text as the label.
Don't show an error before the user has interacted with the field.
Don't make an icon-only Leading/Trailing slot clickable without an aria-label; decorative slots pass clicks to the field.
Don't open a Date/Select popover on a read-only field.
Don't repeat the label as placeholder; show an example or the format (harness: input/placeholder-not-label).
Don't use RichTextField for plain notes (→ TextAreaField) or single-line input (→ InputField).
Don't wire onChange on RichTextField; it reports content through onValueChange (harness: richtext/value-not-onchange).
a11y: The whole field is the click target (padding/icons focus the native field; Select opens).
Errors set aria-invalid and link the message via aria-describedby.
NumberField is role=spinbutton: ↑/↓ step, Enter/blur clamp.
Select and Date pickers: ↓ opens, Escape closes, focus returns to the trigger.
HeadingField multiline is a textarea: Enter never adds a line break; handle it in onKeyDown when Enter should move on.
An invalid field keeps its Negative border while focused and adds the 3px focus ring: error styling never hides focus (WCAG 2.4.7; harness: focus/state-parity).
content: Labels are nouns ("Work email"); errors are sentences with the fix ("Enter a valid email address, like name@company.com").

Every field has a visible label (or an aria-label when the context labels it).
Placeholder shows an example or format, never repeats the label.

search.title: Search
search.purpose: Find or filter content by typing. Like every Zen input it has no Disabled state.
use: Filtering a visible list or table as the user types.
Global/entity search with results below.
avoid: Collecting a form value → InputField.
Picking from a known short list → SelectField or a Chip filter.
api: × appears once there is a value
filter-icon / filter-dropdown trailing is clickable by default (Input Leading/Trailing)
⌘K hint in the trailing slot; ⌘/Ctrl + key focuses the field
do: Describe the scope in the placeholder ("Search components").
Filter live and show an empty state that echoes the query.
Let Enter open the first result; the clear button resets to recent items.
Pair Search with Chip filters in table toolbars. Search fills its container, so give it a Grid column: columns={{ mobile: 1, desktop: "minmax(0, 320px) 1fr" }} with the chips in the second cell.
Debounce remote search (~250ms) and keep the query when results refresh.
Show the result count in an aria-live region ("12 results").
When nothing matches, show an EmptyState that echoes the query and offers “Clear search” (illustration={false} in narrow panels such as sidebars and pickers).
dont: Don't hide search behind an icon on desktop when search is a primary task.
Don't clear the query when results update.
Don't use Disabled; hide Search or keep it Read-only when it is unavailable.
Don't trigger search only on Enter for small, local lists; filter as the user types.
Don't use a vague placeholder ("Type here…").
a11y: type=search; aria-label defaults to the placeholder.
Announce result counts with aria-live.
content: Placeholder: "Search <things>"; empty state: "No <things> match “query”."

Search needs a placeholder that says what is searched, or an aria-label.

segmented.title: Segmented
segmented.purpose: Switch between 2–5 mutually exclusive views or sections of the same content.
use: View switchers (grid ↔ list).
Section switchers with counters (Inbox · Mentions).
avoid: Filtering data → Chip (variant="advanced").
More than 5 options or long labels → Tabs or SelectField.
Form answers → RadioButton group.
api: secondary (default, the common case) · primary (stronger emphasis, e.g. a pricing toggle)
controlled or not (onChange is the deprecated alias)
the option's aria-label names the segment
fills the container; items share it equally and labels ellipsize (automatic inside a Top Navigation control bar)

code only (the Figma container hugs and clips): in a container narrower than its options, e.g. a phone, the control scrolls sideways like Tabs; items keep their width and the selected segment scrolls into view
do: Keep the default level (Secondary), the most common case; set level="primary" only when the switch needs extra emphasis (e.g. a billing-period toggle).
Name the control with aria-label.
Keep labels to one or two words; icon-only items still need a label for assistive tech.
Use badges for counts and hide them at zero.
Keep the selected segment static: no hover and a default cursor, because one option is always selected and re-clicking it does nothing.
Keep 2–5 options (harness: segmented/option-count).
Name icon-only segments with "aria-label" on the option and mark the icon decorative (harness: segmented/icon-only-needs-name).

On mobile, stretch a Segmented to its container (fullWidth) in a Top Navigation control bar, a Bottom Sheet or a narrow panel, so the items share the width equally (harness: segmented/control-bar-full-width).

Elsewhere on a phone, keep the full labels and let a Segmented that outgrows the width scroll sideways; it does so on its own, like Tabs, and keeps the selected segment in view. Use fullWidth only when every label fits its equal share.
dont: Don't use Segmented as a filter.
Don't abbreviate labels or shrink the text to squeeze a Segmented onto a phone; past 5 options or long labels, switch to Tabs or SelectField.
Don't mix icon-only and labelled items in one control.
Don't add a hover or pressed state to the selected segment; it suggests the choice can be undone by clicking it again.
a11y: A labelled group of toggle buttons (aria-pressed); Tab moves between segments, Enter/Space selects.
When the control scrolls, focusing a segment brings it into view; no scrollbar is drawn, as in Tabs.
content: Nouns for sections, no verbs.

badge.title: Badge & Badge-Counter

Unread/notification counts (BadgeCounter).
Removable labels on an item (remove + onRemove).

use: Tables and result lists where position matters ("page 3 of 10").
Inline/Manually themes for data tables with a page-size choice or a jump-to-page field.
avoid: Short lists that fit on one screen; show everything.
Continuous feeds → load more / infinite scroll.
api: primary · secondary (numbered) · inline (page size + range) · manually (jump field + range)
do: Keep the current page visible and marked (aria-current).
Show first and last pages with an ellipsis for long ranges.
In tables, pick the page size with the Inline theme's Chip.
Scroll back to the top of the list after a page change.
dont: Don't paginate lists with only one or two pages.
Don't reset filters or sorting when the page changes.
Don't use numbered pages for unbounded feeds.
Don't paginate fewer than 3 pages (harness: pagination/worth-paging).
a11y: nav with aria-label; the current page has aria-current=page; prev/next are labelled IconButtons that disable at the ends.
The range text updates in an aria-live region.
Under 480px long ranges drop the optional page numbers and keep first · current · last with ellipses; the bar wraps instead of overflowing.
content: Range as “1 - 50 of 100 results”.

rules.summary: Paginate only when there are 3+ pages; otherwise show everything.

Measurable progress → Progress.
Instant loads (< ~300ms); show nothing.

Wrap the loading region in aria-busy=true with a visually hidden “Loading…” status.
Swap to real content in one step.
Respect reduced motion: the pulse turns off (harness: motion/reduced-motion).
dont: Don't show skeletons for content that loads instantly.
Don't use one big block for everything; it hides the structure.
Don't keep a skeleton on screen indefinitely; show an error or empty state.
a11y: Skeleton pieces are aria-hidden; announce loading once on the container (aria-busy + role=status).

Between toolbar groups (vertical, decorative).
Under a total or summary line (High).

Separating every row of a table → row rules in the table itself.
Adding space → use spacing tokens, not an empty line.
api: a Default dashed line steps up to Subtle
do: Use the Default color unless the design explicitly needs more emphasis.
Reserve High for the one line that closes a calculation (receipt totals).
Mark toolbar and label separators decorative when the groups are already labelled.
Let spacing do most of the grouping; add a divider only where groups would otherwise blur.

Don't use a divider as a container border.
Don't draw dashed dividers in Pale — dashed steps up to Subtle automatically.
a11y: Horizontal renders <hr> (role separator); vertical renders role=separator with aria-orientation; decorative dividers are aria-hidden.

inline-message.title: Inline Message
inline-message.purpose: A Subtle-surface message placed inside the content it describes — contextual, persistent until resolved or dismissed.
use: Context for a form or section ("You're editing production").
The result of an action next to where it happened ("Domain verified").
A summary of form errors above the fields.
Theme Custom with your own visual (avatar, logo, thumbnail) for product announcements.
avoid: Page- or app-wide conditions → Alert Banner.
Transient feedback after an action → Toast.
A single field's validation → the field's error text.
Blocking decisions → Dialog.
api: neutral · info · positive · warning · negative · custom
theme icon (Content/<theme>/Light); a node replaces it; Custom takes any visual
do: Place it directly above or beside the content it's about.
Lead with the impact in the title, then the fix in the caption.
Offer at most one action, phrased as a verb ("View plans").
Keep the text Strongest (title) and Base (caption) of the theme; the icon carries the Light highlight.
Use Custom only with a real visual (harness: inline-message/custom-needs-visual).
dont: Don't render an empty message (harness: inline-message/needs-content).
Don't stack several inline messages; merge them or show the most severe.
Don't use Negative for a single invalid field; put the error on the field.
Don't make essential information dismissible.
a11y: role=status; warning and negative use role=alert.
The close control is a labelled button.
Colour is always paired with an icon and text.
content: Title ≤ 1 line; caption says what to do next.

empty-state.title: Empty State
empty-state.purpose: Explains why a screen or region has nothing to show and what the user can do next.
use: First run (no data yet): one Primary action that creates the first item.
No results for a search or filter: echo the query and offer to clear it.
No permission: explain and offer to request access.
avoid: Loading → Skeleton.
Errors that need a retry → Inline Message (negative) with an action.
Tiny regions (a single table cell) → a short line of text.
api: placeholder with a centre icon; a node replaces it; false hides it
do: Say what is empty in the title ("No projects yet", "No results for “tokns”").
Give the next step as a verb in primaryAction (Primary); a way out such as Clear filters or Clear search goes alone in secondaryAction (Tertiary) (harness: empty-state/way-out-tertiary).
Drop the illustration inside lists, tables and cards; keep it for full pages.
Keep the caption to one sentence.
dont: Don't show an Empty State while data is still loading.
Don't leave a first-run screen without an action.
Don't use vague action labels (harness: empty-state/action-label).
Don't use more than two actions.
a11y: The title is a heading (h3) so the state is discoverable; the illustration is aria-hidden.
content: Title: what is empty. Caption: why, or what will appear here. Action: what to do.

stepper.title: Stepper
stepper.purpose: Shows progress through a multi-step, sequential process and where the user is in it.
use: Checkouts, onboarding, imports and setup wizards with 2–7 ordered steps.
Vertical beside the step content when steps have longer titles or captions.
Read-only status trackers (order shipped) with Style=Icon.
avoid: Switching between peer views → Tabs or Segmented.
Showing a percentage → Progress.
A single step → no stepper.
api: earlier = Passed (check), current = Focused (ring), later = Default
State=Error: negative marker, ring and lines
keyboard: Go back to a passed step (onStepClick)
do: Name the process with aria-label (harness: stepper/needs-label).
Keep 2–7 steps with short noun titles (harness: stepper/step-count).
Let users click back to passed steps to edit; keep future steps inert.
Mark a failed step with error and explain the fix next to it (Inline Message).
dont: Don't let users skip ahead to unvisited steps unless every step is optional.
Don't use a stepper for navigation between unrelated pages.
Don't hide the current step's title on small screens; switch to vertical instead.
a11y: Ordered list with aria-label; the current step has aria-current=step; Passed and Error add hidden “(completed)” / “(error)” text.
content: Titles are nouns ("Shipping"); captions add the detail ("Address", "Optional").

rules.summary: A Stepper needs an aria-label naming the process ("Checkout").

slider.title: Slider
slider.purpose: Pick a value from a continuous or stepped range by dragging, where the relative position matters more than the exact number.
use: Volume, brightness, zoom, size — values users tune by feel.
Stepped quantities with visible limits (storage 10–500 GB).
White theme on imagery and media controls.
avoid: Exact numbers users type → NumberField.
A handful of discrete options → Segmented or RadioButton.
On/off → Toggle.
api: small (10px rail, floating 16px dot) · medium (24) · large (32)
value / defaultValue / onValueChange · min · max · step
leading icon inside the fill (Medium/Large); false hides it
do: Use a Solid icon for the leading Icon (it sits inside the filled track): icon-volume-max-solid, icon-sun-solid.
Always name it (harness: slider/needs-name) and give valueText for units ("40%", "120 gigabytes").
Show the current value next to the slider when the number matters.
Use step for quantities with natural increments.
Preview the effect live while dragging (volume, size).
dont: Don't use White at Small — it doesn't exist (harness: slider/white-no-small).
Don't use a slider for precise values without a way to type them.
Don't put two sliders controlling the same value on one screen.
a11y: Native input type=range: ←/→/↑/↓ step, PageUp/PageDown, Home/End; focus ring on the dot; aria-valuetext from valueText.
content: Label the setting ("Volume"), not the action ("Drag to change").

The Slider leading icon uses the Solid style (it sits inside the filled track).

card.title: Card
card.purpose: A surface that groups related content about one subject — a project, a stat, a choice — and can be selected or opened as a whole.
use: Grids of objects users scan and pick (projects, templates, plans).
KPI / stat tiles (Shadow or Flat).
A selectable option with rich content (Active marks the choice).
Framing a List or a group of settings (Border).
avoid: Page sections that are just spacing → layout, not a card.
A single line of content → ListItem.
Rows of comparable data → Table.
Messages → Inline Message.
api: default · alt — Surface/Default or Surface/Alt to suit the page Canvas; unset follows an inherited --zen-card-surface, else default
Surface + 2px Card/Border/Active (active is the deprecated alias)
role=button, Enter/Space; Border steps up to Neutral/Subtle
{ label, icon, onClick } or a node — top-right Small Flat icon button
do: Use one theme per grid; Shadow on the canvas, Border inside another surface, Pale/Semi-Pale on imagery.
Make the whole card clickable when it opens one thing, and name it with aria-label when the content doesn't start with a title.
Use Active for the selected card in a single-choice grid, together with aria-pressed or a radio inside.
Put secondary card actions in the Sub-Action menu.
Pick surface from the page Canvas: default on Canvas/Default, alt on a white Canvas/Alt page (or set --zen-card-surface once on the page scope).

Pricing plans: Border cards in an auto-fit grid; Active marks the current plan, an Accent Badge marks the recommended one, and each card ends with one md CTA pinned to the bottom whose label says what happens (Upgrade to Pro · Switch · Manage plan).
dont: Don't put buttons, links or inputs inside a clickable card (harness: card/clickable-no-nested-controls).
Don't nest cards inside cards.
Don't frame a static card with Subtle — Border uses Pale until the card is clickable (§6).
Don't use Active as decoration; it means selected.
a11y: Clickable cards are one focusable role=button with a visible focus ring; static cards are plain containers.
Keep reading order: title first, then meta.
content: Title first, then one line of meta.

rules.summary: A clickable Card (onClick) is one button: it must not contain buttons, links, inputs or a subAction.

dock-icon.title: Dock Icon
dock-icon.purpose: A round, filled icon tile that identifies an app, category, file type or object.
use: Leading visual of List-Items and Table media cells.
App launchers and integration grids.
Category marks (spending, file types) in Subtle.
Emoji reactions (Theme=Emoji).
avoid: People → Avatar.
Clickable icon controls → IconButton.
Status → Badge.
api: xsmall 24 · small 32 · medium 40 · large 56 · xlarge 80 (Image-Size tokens; glyph Element-Size)
neutral · accent · 15 support colours · inverse · on-color · pale · surface · emoji
role=img name; omit when a text label sits next to it
do: Use Subtle in dense lists and tables; Solid for app tiles and hero marks.
Keep one size per list (Small in tables, Medium in lists).
Leave it decorative (no label) when the name is next to it.
Map colours consistently to categories across the product.
dont: Don't make a Dock Icon a button on its own; wrap it in a labelled control.
Don't use Theme=Emoji without an emoji (harness: dock-icon/emoji-needs-glyph).
Don't use it for people — that's an Avatar.
a11y: Decorative by default (aria-hidden); pass label for a standalone meaningful icon.

list-item.title: List Item
list-item.purpose: One row of a vertical list: a leading visual, a title with an optional caption, and a trailing slot for actions or a passive chevron / value.
use: People, messages, files and settings lists.
Navigation lists that drill down (href / onClick with a passive chevron).
Rows with one or two quick actions (message, add, more) next to the row's own click target.
avoid: Comparable data across several columns → Table.
Choices users toggle in a form → Checkbox / RadioButton / Toggle groups.
Menu options in a popover → Popover items.
Horizontal card grids → Card.
api: Avatar (Image-Size/Medium, 40px), Dock Icon, thumbnail — Figma Leading on/off
Title Body/Base/Bold (one line, truncates) + caption Body/Small/Regular Light (may wrap); children replace the stack
Figma Slot-Actions: Button/Icon-Flat Medium (IconButton appearance="flat" size="md", 40px), gap Small; or a passive chevron, value or Badge
Default / Hover / Pressed from real interaction; Selected = Active/Neutral/Subtle — the Interactive-Background is inset 12px, Corner-Radius/Large

ul wrapper. inset = auto (default) · comfortable (Margin/Comfortable 24px) · compact (Margin/Compact) · none (0). auto follows the layout: 24px full-bleed on a page, 0 inside Modal, Side Panel, Card and a Stack or Box with padding, which already pad their content
keyboard: Move between rows and trailing actions
do: Wrap rows in <List aria-label> so the group is named.
Make the whole row the target (onClick / href) when it opens one thing; for drill-down add a passive chevron.

Put quick actions in the trailing slot as Button/Icon-Flat Medium (IconButton appearance="flat" size="md") with an aria-label. They work on clickable rows too — Figma keeps the trailing action in Hover, Pressed and Selected — and stay separate targets that don't open the row.
Keep to one or two trailing actions; move the rest into a More (…) menu.
Let the title truncate on one line; keep the caption short (it may wrap to a second line).
Mark the current row with selected (Active/Neutral/Subtle), not a custom fill.

Let the row inset follow the layout: full-bleed lists on a page keep 24px, lists inside a Modal, Side Panel or Card line up with the container's content (inset auto → none) and the hover fill bleeds into its padding. Set inset only when the layout needs something else.
Split long settings into groups: a visible heading per group and one List per group named after it (aria-label or aria-labelledby).

In a bordered Card, derive the container from the row's hover fill (Corner-Radius/Large): card padding Padding/2XSmall (4) top and bottom, row inset Padding/Small + Padding/2XSmall (16), card radius Corner-Radius/XLarge (= Large + 4). The fill then sits 4 from every edge with concentric corners in every radius mode.
dont: Don't make only the chevron or a trailing button the way to open the row — the whole row is the target.
Don't put a Toggle or Checkbox on a clickable row: the row click and the switch compete. Make the row flip the switch, or keep the row static (harness: list-item/clickable-row-toggle).
Don't use Small or text buttons in the trailing slot; trailing actions are Medium icon buttons (harness: list-item/trailing-button-medium).
Don't mix leading sizes in one list — row heights stop lining up.
Don't override .zen-list-item padding for spacing — use <List inset> or --zen-list-inset on the container (harness: list-item/inset-not-padding).
Don't use a list for data users compare across columns.
Don't hand-build rows (a div with a Text and a Badge or Button); use ListItem so padding, hit area and focus are consistent.
a11y: A clickable row is one <button>/<a> covering the row with a visible focus ring; selected rows expose aria-pressed / aria-current.
Trailing actions are separate buttons after the row in the tab order, each named by aria-label; activating them never triggers the row.
content: Title = the object's name; caption = the most useful fact (role, last message, size).

rules.summary: List rows take their horizontal inset from the layout (List inset / --zen-list-inset), never a padding override on .zen-list-item — a fixed padding double-indents rows inside Modals, Side Panels and Cards.
A clickable row (onClick/href) doesn't also carry a Toggle or Checkbox — the row click and the switch compete. Trailing icon buttons are fine (Figma Slot-Actions).
Buttons in a List-Item trailing slot are size Medium (md).
Counts agree with their noun (1 item · 2 items): build the phrase with a plural helper, never `{list.length} items`.

table.title: Table
table.purpose: Rows of structured records that users scan, compare, sort and act on.
use: Data with several comparable attributes per record (members, invoices, files).
Bulk actions on selected rows.
Sorting by a column.
Quick corrections of a few fields (stock, owner, status, tags) without leaving the list → editable columns.
avoid: One or two attributes per item → List Item.
Layout grids → CSS grid.
Key/value details of one record → a description list.
Editing many fields of one record, or edits that need review → a form or Side Panel (use onOpen to get there).
api: columns[] {id, header, align, width, sortable, icon, cell}
checkbox column; select-all is indeterminate when partial
column.edit {type: text · number · select · tags, value, onCommit, validate, disabled, options, suggestions, multiline}
Figma Table/Cell/Default State=Edit · Editabled-Cell; Focused ring Focus/Accent/Subtle
Figma Open-Button: XSmall Tertiary “Open” on row hover
Text / Avatar-Photo-Icon-Dock / Trend / Actions cells; Badge, Tag, ProgressBar go in directly
TableText · TableMedia · TableBadges · TableTags · TableTrend · TableActions

Figma Primitives/Table/Cell/*: Text-Cell (Body/Base Regular|Bold + Subtext Caption/Regular 11/16, gap 3XSmall); media size follows Subtext — Avatar/Photo-Cell 24px (Avatar XSmall) without a caption, 32px (Small) with one; Basic-Icon-Cell 20px (Icon base) / 28px (Icon lg); Dock-Icon-Cell Dock Icon XSmall 24px / Small 32px — media gap Small; Badge-Cell and Trend-Cell Badge Medium; Tag-Cell Tag; Items gap 2XSmall; Group-Avatar-Cell Avatar/Stack Small; Actions-Cell Button/Icon-Flat Medium, gap XSmall; Progress-Cell Progress-Bar
keyboard: Move between sort buttons, checkboxes and actions
Sort by a column; toggle a row checkbox
Save and move to the next / previous cell
Leave; keeps a valid value, reverts an invalid one
do: Name the table (caption or aria-label; harness: table/needs-name).
Right-align numbers and amounts; keep text left.
Give each row one primary text (bold) and at most one caption.

Put row actions in the last column (TableActions) as Button/Icon-Flat Medium (IconButton appearance="flat" level="primary"; a ⋯ Menu trigger for several) and bulk actions above the table (harness: table/actions-flat).
Show an Empty State row when filters return nothing.
Make only the fields people routinely correct editable; keep IDs, computed and audit columns read-only.
Wire onCommit to save, and validate numbers and required text; the error stays in the cell until fixed (harness: table/editor-needs-commit, table/editor-number-validate).
Right-align number editors like the numbers they edit (harness: table/editor-number-right).
Use select for closed sets and tags for open sets; lock rows that can't change with edit.disabled.
Offer onOpen when the full record needs a detail view.
Let clickable content inside an editable cell (Tag onClick, links, buttons) keep its own action — clicking the cell around it edits. Leave room (padding, gaps) so the edit target stays easy to hit.
Title a table with Heading/4: pass it as `caption` (rendered as Heading/4), or place a Heading/4 directly above the table (harness: table/title-heading-4).

Build cells from the cell primitives at their Figma sizes: Badge Medium (not Small) in Badge/Trend cells, media sized by Subtext (Avatar XSmall → Small and Icon base → lg and Dock Icon XSmall → Small when a caption is on) (harness: table/media-size-by-subtext), Avatar/Stack Small for groups.
dont: Don't make selectable or sortable tables without handlers (harness: table/interaction-needs-handler).
Don't wrap long text in every cell; truncate and show the full value on the detail view.
Don't use colour alone for status — use a Badge with text.
Don't make every cell editable — it turns the table into a spreadsheet and invites accidental edits.
Don't commit on every keystroke; the editor saves on Enter, Tab, Escape (valid values) or clicking another cell.
Don't hide the saved result: show the new value immediately and confirm or undo in a Toast when the change is significant.
Don't title a table with a Body/…/Bold label; it reads as a row label, not a section title. Use Heading/4.
a11y: Native table semantics: th scope=col, aria-sort on sortable headers, sort buttons, labelled row checkboxes; the wrapper scrolls horizontally on small screens.

Editable cells (Notion-style): one click or press starts editing; Enter / F2 / typing / arrows work on a focused cell. Enter saves; Tab and Shift+Tab save and move; clicking another cell saves and edits it; Escape leaves and keeps the typed value (reverts if it fails validation). Text grows in an overlay (Shift+Enter adds a line when edit.multiline); select is a searchable list (type to filter, Enter picks the top match); tags: Enter picks the first suggestion or creates the tag, Backspace on an empty input removes the last. Validation errors use role=alert; the layout never shifts.
Clickable content inside an editable cell is its own Tab stop; Enter on it runs its action, Enter on the cell edits.
After an edit ends (Enter, Escape, or picking an option), focus returns to the cell without a ring so the value reads cleanly; the ring comes back as soon as arrow keys or Tab move to another cell.
content: Headers are short nouns; units go in the header ("Amount (USD)"), not every cell.

rules.summary: Row actions in TableActions are Button/Icon-Flat Medium (IconButton appearance="flat" level="primary"), so rows don't fill with outlined buttons.
A table's title is Heading/4 — via the Table `caption` or a Heading/4 Text or Heading directly above the <Table>.
A Table is named by a caption or aria-label.
Selectable tables need onSelectionChange; sortable columns need onSortChange.

TableMedia follows the Figma cell primitives: with a caption (Subtext=Yes) Avatar/Photo is Small 32px and a basic Icon lg 28px; without one Avatar is XSmall 24px and Icon base 20px; Dock Icon follows Avatar (XSmall 24px → Small 32px with a caption).
An editable column (edit: { … }) saves through onCommit; without it edits are silently lost.

borders.title: Container borders (Subtle vs Pale)
borders.purpose: Pick the border of a closed container (a stroke or ring enclosing a box on all sides) by whether the box can be acted on: Subtle for actionable, Pale for non-actionable. Dashed strokes are always at least Subtle.

Subtle for every dashed line or stroke — dashed dividers, dashed empty states and drop zones, the Read-only field's dash — even on a static box (a dash has less ink, so Pale is too faint).

A Divider defaults to Pale; Medium (Subtle) and High (Solid) only when the design calls for more.
Strokes around media — avatars, photos, visuals, illustrations, graphics, thumbnails: not covered (Subtle allowed).
Component border tokens (Button-Tertiary, Chip-Secondary, Tag, Checkbox, Radio-Button, Segmented-Item) — use them instead of raw Neutral tokens.

Don't give a Pale container border hover or pressed feedback.
Don't draw a dashed line or stroke with Pale or a raw colour.
Don't pick the token by how strong you want the line to look.
Don't hard-code a border colour in component CSS; use tokens (harness: color/token-only).

background-layers.title: Background layers (Canvas → Popover)

Surface — cards and containers placed on the Canvas. Choose surface-default or surface-alt to suit the style of the page (e.g. white cards on a canvas-default page; a softer surface-alt on a canvas-alt page). Canvas-alt and surface-default are the same colour, so a surface-default box on a canvas-alt page always gets a border (§11).

Canvas-flat + Surface-flat — for flat designs: top and bottom navigation containers on a canvas-flat page use surface-flat, so the bar and the page read as one seamless surface in both light and dark mode.
Other colours — component fills (Neutral/Subtle, Support/*, Solid, states) sit on Surface or Canvas.
Container — only Modal/Dialog, Modal/Forms and Bottom-Sheet panels.
Popover — the top layer: popovers, menus, dropdowns, tooltips, date pickers, flyouts, toasts.
avoid: Painting a component with Canvas — Canvas is the page, components start at Surface.
Using Container for an in-page card, or Popover for an in-flow panel — both belong to floating layers.
api: cards, panels, sidebars on the page; -flat = top/bottom navigation on a canvas-flat page
Popover, menus, tooltips, pickers, flyouts, toasts

Place cards on the page with Surface; match default/alt to the page style.
On a canvas-flat page, give top and bottom navigation surface-flat so both modes stay seamless.
Only raise a box to Container or Popover when it actually floats above the page (modal, sheet, overlay).

Don't cast a drop shadow from a Subtle, Pale or Surface-Alt background, even where Figma pairs one with Shadow/Action/* (harness: surface/no-shadow-on-tinted).

Don't use surface-flat for cards; it is for navigation on a flat page (harness: layer/surface-flat-is-navigation).

Don't use Background/Popover for in-flow content (harness: layer/popover-is-overlay).

Canvas is only the page layer; components never paint Canvas — cards and containers on the page use Surface.
Surface/Flat is for top/bottom navigation containers on a Canvas/Flat page, so both modes read as one seamless surface.
A Subtle / Pale / Surface-Alt background never casts a drop shadow (inset effects and 0 0 0 Npx rings are fine); guard component shadows with <bg>-shadow-off.

content-colors.title: Content colours (text & icons)
content-colors.purpose: Text and icon colours share the Color/Content tokens, but the level depends on the family: neutral families map Strongest/Base/Light to the Primary/Secondary/Tertiary text roles; colour families use Strongest/Base for normal text on Subtle backgrounds and Light only for highlights; the Lights group (colours referencing Sky, Mint, Yellow or Zen) never uses Light for text.

Colour families — Accent, Info, Positive, Negative, Warning and every Support/* colour: Strongest and Base are regular text, the Primary and Secondary levels, placed on that colour's Subtle background (subtle Badge, Tag, Alert, callout).
Colour Light: text or icons that must stand out as a highlight — status icons, a success/error hint, a positive or negative delta, a highlighted keyword.

Lights group — every family whose tokens reference the Sky, Mint, Yellow or Zen scales (similar low contrast); today Accent (Zen), Warning (Yellow) and Support/Yellow: text is Base at most (Strongest or Base); Light is only for icons. The harness derives the group from tokens.css.

Disabled and placeholder text → Content/Disabled and Content/Placeholder (or the overlay/inverse equivalents).
Links → Content/Hyperlink/*.

accent · info · positive · negative · warning · support-*

families referencing Sky · Mint · Yellow · Zen (today: accent · warning · support-yellow)

Don't use neutral Light for titles or primary values.

form.title: Form
form.purpose: Collect a set of values and submit them. Form is a <form noValidate> laid out as a Stack; useFormState holds values and errors and binds every Zen field in one spread; FormField labels custom controls, FormFieldset groups choices and FormActions is the footer row.

The Cancel + submit footer of a page or card form → FormActions (it stacks on phones and can stick to the bottom).

Settings that apply at once → Toggle, outside any Form.
A single inline edit (rename a title) → HeadingField, saved on blur.
Filtering a list → Search and Chip filters; nothing to submit.

Write Tertiary (Cancel) first and Primary (type="submit", named for the outcome) last in FormActions: Primary lands on the right, or on top when the actions stack (harness: form/actions-order, form/submit-button).

Put field errors from the server on the field with setError; show a failed request (thrown by onSubmit, in submitError) in a Negative InlineMessage with a Try again action, keeping every value.
Show progress on the submit button while isSubmitting ("Saving…").
On a phone, use sticky FormActions so the main action stays above the home indicator while the fields scroll.
Mark the exception: when most fields are required, label only the optional ones (labelOptional / optional).

Wrap each Zen field in its <Controller> and map value, the field's change callback (onValueChange(value) on every Zen field — or onChange(event) on the text fields — and onCheckedChange(checked) on Checkbox and Toggle), onBlur and error={fieldState.error?.message}; <Form onSubmit={handleSubmit(onValid)}> still focuses the first invalid field and announces the count.

Don't show an error while someone is still typing a new value; wait until they leave the field or submit.
Don't put Toggles in a Form that is saved later; use a Checkbox, and keep instant Toggles outside the Form (harness: form/toggle-outside-form).
Don't wrap InputField, SelectField & co. in FormField; they already have label, helpText and error.

Don't clear the fields after a failed submit, and don't use the placeholder as the label or for instructions.

A failed submit moves focus to the first invalid field (scrolled to the middle) and announces "N fields need attention" in a polite live region; handleSubmit also focuses when passed to ModalForm or a plain <form>.

Submit labels name the outcome ("Create account", "Save changes", "Send invite"); progress labels end with an ellipsis ("Saving…").
Legends are short nouns or phrases ("Delivery", "Email me about").

Other sites (docs, status page) in a new tab with external.

One or two actions → show them as buttons.

On a phone, keep menus to a few short actions; longer lists, or ones that need a title, are an Action BottomSheet.

provider.title: ZenProvider (app root)

Switching a region to another mode (a dark hero, a mobile preview) with a nested provider.
Following the OS colour scheme with theme="system".

Setting data-* attributes by hand → pass them as ZenProvider props.
Painting a card or panel → Card, Box or a Surface token; ZenProvider paints Canvas (the page).

One button under a short form → a plain Button row after the fields.
api: vertical (default, phones: Large full-width buttons, Primary on top) · horizontal (desktop: summary at the start, Tertiary · Primary at the end; under 480px the buttons split the row)
sticky (default: pinned to the bottom of the scroll area, settles at the end) · fixed (viewport; an in-flow spacer keeps the end reachable) · static
default (Surface/Default + Pale top rule) · alt (Surface/Alt) · none; never a drop shadow
{ label, onClick, level?, disabled?, startIcon?, type?, form? }: sized (lg vertical, md horizontal) and ordered for you
Buttons in visual order: Primary first when vertical, last when horizontal
a total, selection count or status line; wrap text that changes in role="status"
bottom padding = max(Padding/Small, --zen-safe-area-bottom or env(safe-area-inset-bottom) + Padding/XSmall)
keyboard: Move through the actions in visual order (Primary first when vertical, last when horizontal)
do: Hold one Primary, the screen's main action (harness: action-bar/one-primary).
On phones keep it vertical: Large full-width buttons, Primary on top, at most one Tertiary below (harness: action-bar/full-width-size, action-bar/primary-order).
Prefer primaryAction / secondaryAction: they get the right size and order in both directions, so one set of actions serves phone and desktop.
Place a sticky bar as the last child of the scrolling content, inside the form it submits (type: "submit").
Say what the actions act on in the summary ("2 prints · $96.00", "3 unsaved changes") and announce changes with role="status".
Disable the Primary only while its precondition is unmet, and say why in the summary ("No changes to save yet").
dont: Don't put two Primary buttons in the bar, or a Secondary as the alternative.
Don't use small buttons (2xs · xs · sm) in a vertical bar; stretched thin buttons read as fields.
Don't add a drop shadow or a tinted fill; the Pale top rule separates the bar.
Don't stack more than two actions on a phone; move the rest into the page or a More menu.
Don't use surface="none" on a sticky or fixed bar; the content would scroll visibly under the buttons.
Don't pad the page for the home indicator yourself; the bar already clears the safe area.
a11y: Buttons keep their visual order in the DOM, so Tab follows what people see; primaryAction / secondaryAction are reordered per direction.
With aria-label ("Order actions") the bar is a named group; without one it adds no extra landmark.
Announce summary changes (added to cart, saved) with role="status".
A sticky bar stays below open popovers (z-index 3 vs. 4), so a dropdown near the bottom opens over it.
content: Labels name the outcome with a verb: "Add to cart", "Save changes", "Place order · $86.40"; never "OK" or "Submit".
The Tertiary is a real alternative ("Save for later", "Undo changes"), not a second way to do the Primary.

rules.summary: An Action Bar holds one Primary, the screen's main action; everything else is Tertiary (or Danger when irreversible).
Button children follow the visual order: Primary first (on top) in a vertical bar, last (at the end) in a horizontal one. primaryAction / secondaryAction are ordered for you.
A vertical Action Bar stretches its buttons across the width, so they are size lg (the mobile footer CTA), never 2xs · xs · sm.

Every interaction a Zen control offers works: no no-op handlers (`() => {}`, `() => undefined`), which leave a field that ignores typing and ↑/↓ or a Dismiss that stays. Chat has chat/no-locked-interaction.

Repo examples, playgrounds and templates: every action does something when pressed. Flags a `Button` or `<button>` without onClick / href / type="submit" (IconButton: icon-button/needs-action), an action object ({ icon, label }) in leading, trailing, action, primaryAction, secondaryAction, subAction or actions without onClick, and pressable items whose list has no onSelect / onNavigate / onItemClick / onValueChange. Documented defaults pass: Dialog, ModalForm, SidePanel and BottomSheet actions close the overlay; a Menu opens from its trigger. Apps are not judged.

image.title: Image & Thumbnail
image.purpose: Shows a picture in a ratio frame that keeps its size while loading (Skeleton) and fails gracefully (neutral placeholder, alt kept). Thumbnail is the fixed square for list rows, tables and pickers.
use: Product, listing and article photos in cards and detail pages (Image with a ratio).
Galleries and feeds, with a caption (figure/figcaption) when the picture needs a credit or context.
Pictures in ListItem leading slots, Table media cells and pickers (Thumbnail on the Image-Size scale).
avoid: People → Avatar (initials fallback, status, stacks).
App or category symbols → DockIcon or Icon.
File types → FileIcon.
Decorative backgrounds → CSS on the container.
api: 1:1 · 4:3 · 3:2 · 16:9 · 3:4 or width ÷ height; unset = the picture's own ratio (4:3 while loading)
cover (default, crops) · contain (the whole picture on Neutral/Pale)
lazy (default) · eager for the first picture on screen
undefined → Skeleton; a load error → placeholder with icon-image-line, alt stays its name
rounded (radius steps with the size, like Avatar Square) · circle · square
do: Always pass alt: what the picture shows in context; alt="" only when it is decorative or text beside it names it (harness: image/needs-alt).
Set ratio so the frame keeps its size while loading and nothing jumps when the picture arrives.
Use loading="eager" only for the first picture on screen; keep the rest lazy.
Use Thumbnail md (40) in ListItem leading slots, sm (32) in captioned Table cells and xs (24) in plain ones.
When a picture fails, keep the frame and offer a way forward nearby (Try again, Replace).
Use fit="contain" for logos, documents and cut-outs that must not be cropped.
dont: Don't use a file name or "image of…" as alt (harness: image/alt-describes).
Don't repeat the caption or the row title in alt; screen readers would read it twice.
Don't size a picture with a fixed width and height; give it a ratio and let it fill its container.
Don't use Thumbnail for people; Avatar has initials, status and stacks.
Don't put text over a picture without a scrim or an overlay type that keeps it readable.
a11y: Image renders a native img (a figure with figcaption when captioned); alt is required by the type.
The loading Skeleton is aria-hidden; a failed picture's placeholder is role="img" named by alt (hidden when alt="").
A Thumbnail inside a button (a gallery strip) takes its name from the button: alt="" on the Thumbnail, aria-label and aria-pressed on the button.
content: Alt text is one short, specific sentence ("White houses and a windmill by the sea"), without "image of".
Captions add what the picture can't: place, credit, size ("Bridge at dusk · 50 × 40 cm print").
refs: W3C WAI — An alt decision tree

rules.summary: Image and Thumbnail always carry alt: what the picture shows, or alt="" when it is decorative or the text beside it already names it.
alt describes the picture in context: never a file name, and never "image of…" / "photo of…" (screen readers already announce an image).

visually-hidden.title: Visually Hidden
visually-hidden.purpose: Adds text that only assistive technology reads: names for icon-only table headers, context for repeated links, status announcements, hidden headings and skip links that appear on focus.
use: Column headers that show only an icon or nothing (Actions, Starred).
Context that makes repeated labels unique ("Read more about …", "Edit email").
Status messages for changes shown only visually (role="status": "Link copied to the clipboard").
Skip links (as="a" + focusable) and headings that name a region for screen-reader navigation.
avoid: Naming an icon-only button → IconButton aria-label (it also shows the name as a tooltip).
Naming a field → its label, or aria-label when the context labels it.
Hiding content from everyone → don't render it.
Hiding decoration from screen readers → aria-hidden.
api: span (default, inline) · div · p · label · legend · a · h1–h6
shows the content while it, or a link inside it, has focus: a Surface pill at the top-start corner (skip links)
role="status" for announcements; id for aria-labelledby / aria-describedby
keyboard: Follow the skip link; focus moves to the main content
do: Start hidden text that continues a visible label with a space and no punctuation (`Edit<VisuallyHidden> email</VisuallyHidden>`) so the name reads as one phrase.
Render a status region from the start, empty, then change its text; a region inserted together with its message is often not announced.
Make the skip link the first focusable element of the page and point it at the main content (`tabIndex={-1}`).
Keep the visible label inside the accessible name (WCAG 2.5.3): add words, never replace them.
dont: Don't hide a link or control without focusable; keyboard users would land on something invisible (harness: visually-hidden/focusable-shows).
Don't stuff keywords or long instructions into hidden text; screen-reader users hear every word.
Don't use display:none, visibility:hidden or the hidden attribute for screen-reader text; they remove it from the accessibility tree.
Don't hide a heading sighted people need too; show it.
a11y: The text is clipped to a 1px box (clip-path) and taken out of the flow, but stays in the accessibility tree and in-page search.
Browsers insert a space before out-of-flow text when they build a name, so begin the hidden part with a space.
A focused skip link shows a Surface pill with a Subtle ring and the Focus/Accent outline (WCAG 2.4.1 Bypass Blocks, 2.4.7 Focus Visible).
content: Write hidden text as it will be heard: "Actions", " about Choosing a paper for photo prints", "Link copied to the clipboard".
refs: WebAIM — Invisible content just for screen reader users

rules.summary: Hidden content that takes keyboard focus (a skip link, a button) needs focusable, so it becomes visible while focused (WCAG 2.4.7).
